questions.stem: A car engine burns petrol (hydrocarbons) at high temperatures. Which pollutant is produced NOT from the fuel itself, but from the nitrogen and oxygen in the air?

options.text: Carbon dioxide
Carbon monoxide
Nitrogen oxides (NOₓ)
Sulfur dioxide

questions.explanation: At the high temperatures inside a car engine, nitrogen (N₂) and oxygen (O₂) from the air react together to form nitrogen oxides (NO and NO₂, collectively called NOₓ). Carbon dioxide and carbon monoxide come from the carbon in the fuel, and sulfur dioxide comes from sulfur impurities in the fuel. Nitrogen oxides are unique in coming from the air itself.

questions.stem: Carbon monoxide (CO) is called a 'silent killer' because it is colourless and odourless. How does it cause harm to humans?

options.text: It reacts with the lungs to form carbonic acid
It binds to haemoglobin in red blood cells more strongly than oxygen, reducing the blood's ability to carry oxygen
It dissolves in water in the lungs and causes drowning
It makes the air more flammable

questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide binds to haemoglobin about 200 times more strongly than oxygen does, forming carboxyhaemoglobin. This prevents haemoglobin from carrying oxygen to body tissues. Even small concentrations can be dangerous because the binding is essentially irreversible. This is why CO detectors are important in homes with gas appliances and why car exhaust in enclosed spaces is lethal.

questions.stem: Catalytic converters in car exhaust systems reduce harmful emissions. Which harmful gases are converted, and what are the less harmful products?

options.text: CO₂ and H₂O are converted to carbon and hydrogen
CO and NOₓ are converted to CO₂ and N₂
N₂ and O₂ are converted to NO₂
SO₂ and CO₂ are converted to sulfur and carbon

questions.explanation: Catalytic converters contain platinum and rhodium catalysts that promote two key reactions: (1) carbon monoxide is oxidised to less harmful carbon dioxide: 2CO + O₂ → 2CO₂, and (2) nitrogen oxides are reduced to harmless nitrogen gas: 2NO + 2CO → N₂ + 2CO₂. This converts two toxic pollutants into two relatively harmless gases.

questions.stem: Sulfur dioxide (SO₂) is released when fossil fuels containing sulfur impurities are burned. A power station wants to reduce its SO₂ emissions. Which method would be effective?

options.text: Burning the fuel at a higher temperature
Using flue gas desulfurisation, where SO₂ is removed by reacting it with calcium oxide or calcium carbonate
Adding more air to the combustion chamber
Building a taller chimney to disperse the SO₂

questions.explanation: Flue gas desulfurisation (FGD) uses calcium oxide (CaO) or calcium carbonate (CaCO₃) to react with SO₂ before it leaves the chimney: CaO + SO₂ → CaSO₃. This neutralises the acidic SO₂ gas. The product (calcium sulfite/sulfate) can be used to make plasterboard. A taller chimney only spreads the pollution more widely rather than removing it.

questions.stem: Particulate matter (soot and tiny particles) from diesel engines and coal burning is linked to health problems. How do particulates cause damage?

options.text: They make the air smell bad
They are deposited in the lungs, causing irritation, worsening asthma, and increasing the risk of respiratory and cardiovascular diseases
They only damage buildings, not people
They block sunlight completely, causing vitamin D deficiency

questions.explanation: Fine particulates (PM2.5 — particles smaller than 2.5 micrometres) are especially dangerous because they can penetrate deep into the lungs and even enter the bloodstream. They cause inflammation in the airways, aggravate conditions like asthma and bronchitis, and long-term exposure increases the risk of lung cancer and heart disease. Particulates also reduce visibility and cause global dimming.
